## Why

Goal 3: record a decision with a rationale and a link to the question it
answers.

## Files

- `internal/commands/decide.go`: decide, reject and withdraw.
- `internal/cli/cli.go`: register the three subcommands.
- `internal/cli/decide_test.go`.

## Failing tests

End-to-end CLI tests call `cli.Run` in a fresh `t.TempDir()` store (with
`t.Chdir`, which rules out `t.Parallel`, or a root option the implementer adds
and records under C32), with a fixed clock where dates matter.

- `adj decide ID OPTION --why TEXT` sets status `decided`, `decision` (the
  option label), `rationale`, `decided_at` and `decided_by`, appends one
  history entry, and rewrites the record in place.
- `adj decide ID --text TEXT --why TEXT` records a free-text decision.
- An OPTION that is not one of the record's options, both OPTION and `--text`,
  neither of them, or no `--why` exits non-zero and leaves the record unchanged.
- `adj reject ID --why TEXT` and `adj withdraw ID --why TEXT` set `rejected` /
  `withdrawn`, record the reason, and append history.
- Each of the three on a record that is not `open`, or on an unknown ID, exits
  non-zero and changes nothing.

## Implement

1. Call the model transitions from S03 and `store.Update` from S05.
2. How `decided_by` is supplied (flag, config or environment): implementer
   decides and records it (C32), reusing the `asked_by` mechanism from S06
   where it fits. Where reject and withdraw store the reason (for example
   `rationale`): same rule.
3. Owner-only decide is a convention (C27): `adj` records `decided_by` and does
   not try to block anyone.
